registryLegalName: Application for a Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity, RCW 9.97.020

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: No state, county or municipal department, board, officer or agency authorised to assess the qualifications of an applicant for a licence, certificate of authority, qualification to engage in a profession or business, or admission to a qualifying examination may disqualify a qualified applicant solely on the basis of criminal history where the applicant holds a certificate of restoration of opportunity and meets all other statutory and regulatory requirements, except as required by federal law or as exempted. The exemptions are extensive: criminal justice agencies as defined in the Washington Criminal Records Privacy Act and the Washington State Bar Association are exempt outright, and the section does not apply to the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators and the other categories the section lists.

Closes the set of qualified courts: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication.
The superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication may not decline to consider the application.

Imposes the duty under which the Administrative Office of the Courts produced the statewide certificate of restoration of opportunity form set. Subsection (11)(b) uses the word "sample", which points toward pattern rather than mandatory status, but the governing court rule was not read.

Treats an issued certificate as part of the criminal history a sentencing court sees, confirming that a certificate is a recognised instrument rather than an informal document — and that it does not remove the conviction.

counselFlags: A certificate of restoration of opportunity operates on the collateral consequences of a conviction, not on the record itself. It does not vacate, seal or expunge anything, and RCW 9.94A.030(11) treats an issued certificate as part of the criminal history a sentencing court sees. A participant seeking record relief needs a different route.

Venue is a closed statutory set under RCW 9.97.010(2): the superior court where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county — the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court.

The RCW 9.97.020 exemptions are extensive and must be encoded before any screening: criminal justice agencies as defined in the Washington Criminal Records Privacy Act and the Washington State Bar Association are exempt outright, and the section does not apply to the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators and the other categories the section lists. A certificate does not help a participant whose target occupation sits in an exemption.

No verification or notarization statute is identified for an RCW 9.97.020 application, and verification is in any event a feature of the Administrative Office of the Courts CRO form set rather than of a drafted pleading. Nothing is filled.
Filing fee: no fee amount is established at source for a certificate of restoration of opportunity application. No amount may be stated to a participant; confirm with the superior court clerk.

Form status unresolved: whether the Administrative Office of the Courts CRO forms are mandatory forms a superior court must accept and a filer must use, pattern forms a filer may adapt, or optional, is unresolved. It decides whether this route is an official-PDF fill or a conforming custom pleading, and it is not answered by any committed source.
Local requirements vary: the Washington Courts local-rule warning means some counties impose additional local requirements. Which counties, and what they require, was not established at source.
A certificate does not restore firearm rights. RCW 9.41.110 is carried in the authority list for this track and firearm eligibility is governed separately.

registryExcerpt.legalName: Application for a Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity, RCW 9.97.020
registryExcerpt.publicName: Get a Washington court certificate that stops most licensing bodies disqualifying you for your record
registryExcerpt.venue: A qualified court, and RCW 9.97.010(2) closes the set: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication; the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court. Because the set is closed and statutory, one statewide packet serves the whole state as to venue and the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication, because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that court may not decline to consider the application.
registryExcerpt.destinationName: The superior court of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2)

waitingPeriods.condition: Misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour, probation or other noncustodial sentence

waitingPeriods.duration: Eighteen months from release from total or partial confinement.
Two years from sentencing on a noncustodial sentence, or two years from release from total or partial confinement.

waitingPeriods.condition: Violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030
waitingPeriods.duration: Five years from sentencing on a noncustodial sentence, or five years from release from total or partial confinement.

exclusions: Any person who has ever been convicted of a class A felony, or an attempt, criminal solicitation of, or criminal conspiracy to commit a class A felony.

Any person who has ever been convicted of a sex offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or a crime that includes sexual motivation under RCW 9.94A.835, RCW 13.40.135 or RCW 9.94A.535(3)(f), or extortion in the first degree.
Any applicant who has not reached the applicable point on the RCW 9.97.010(1)(a) scale.

Any applicant not in compliance with sentencing requirements including legal financial obligations, unless on a compliant payment plan or with good cause established with the court for non-compliance.

The professions and bodies the section does not reach: criminal justice agencies and the Washington State Bar Association, and the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators, receivers, teachers, notaries public, real estate brokers and salespersons, security guards, and the vulnerable adult care providers the section carves out.
Firearm rights and firearm dealer licence eligibility, which the section expressly does not restore.
Removal of a protection order, which the section expressly does not require.

negativeFixtureDisposition.reason: No component of this track is drafted: componentInventory is blocked track-wide, and the verifier bars fixtures/, rendered/ and participant-instructions.md for a blocked_pleading track. There is no render against which a negative fixture could assert anything, and authoring one would mean drafting the very pleading the recorded dependency says cannot be drafted. The anti-invention contract for this track is carried by that dependency, not by a fixture.
negativeFixtureDisposition.revisitWhen: Two distinct items, neither committed. (1) The Washington court rule governing the status of Administrative Office of the Courts forms — whether a superior court must accept them and a filer must use them. The registry records that the statutory word "sample" in RCW 9.97.020(11)(b) points toward pattern rather than mandatory, but that the governing court rule was not read and the memo does not guess. (2) The five CRO binaries (CRO 01.0100, 01.0200, 01.0300, 01.0600, 01.0700) have not been acquired, pinned or measured, and no Washington source-materialization receipt exists for them — recorded as a second build-level dependency owned by the source-acquisition lane.

dependencies.barsDraftingBecause: A complete statewide official form set already exists for this exact application. Drafting a custom petition, notice, proof of service or order would replicate CRO 01.0100, 01.0200, 01.0300 and 01.0700 respectively. If the forms turn out to be mandatory, a replica would be flatly wrong; if they are pattern forms, the correct output is a pleading conforming to forms that have not yet been acquired or measured, which cannot be done without them.
